```{r libraries, message = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250724)
set.seed(20250724)
```

Ramesh et al. (2025) modelled the natural history of autosomal dominant
tubulointerstitial kidney disease (ADTKD) in adults from the Wake Forest
inherited-kidney-disease registry. The two genetic forms, UMOD (uromodulin) and
MUC1 (mucin-1), were modelled separately, and for each form the paper fitted
two independent models: a nonlinear mixed-effects model of eGFR against age,
and a parametric time-to-event model of the age at kidney failure. The package
therefore ships four model files that share this vignette:

```{r load_models}
umod_egfr <- nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("Ramesh_2025_adtkd_umod_egfr")
muc1_egfr <- nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("Ramesh_2025_adtkd_muc1_egfr")
umod_kf <- nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("Ramesh_2025_adtkd_umod_kf")
muc1_kf <- nlmixr2lib::readModelDb("Ramesh_2025_adtkd_muc1_kf")
```

Reference: Ramesh SS, Rogge M, Kidd KO, Williams AH, Yoon DY, Roignot J,
Blakeslee K, Bleyer AJ, Kim S (2025). Quantifying clinical and genetic factors
influencing rate and severity of autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney
disease progression. *J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn* 52(4):41.
[doi:10.1007/s10928-025-09989-0](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-025-09989-0)

There is no drug in these models. The model time is the subject's **age in
years**, so a simulation data set carries age in its `time` column, has no
dosing rows, and supplies the two time-fixed covariates measured at the first
clinic visit: `CRCL_BASE` (eGFR at the first visit, mL/min/1.73 m^2) and
`AGE_BASE` (age at the first visit, years). The kidney-failure model for UMOD
also needs `SEXF`.

## Population

The analysis data set held 6,447 visits from 604 adults aged 18-80 years:
371 with ADTKD-UMOD and 233 with ADTKD-MUC1 (Table 1). The median follow-up
was 9 years. In the UMOD group 215 were female, the median age at the first
clinic visit was 36.8 years (95% interval 18.3-58.9) and the median eGFR at
that visit was 45.4 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (14.6-94.8); 105 reached kidney failure.
In the MUC1 group 142 were female, the median age at the first visit was 37.7
years (20.6-65.0), the median first-visit eGFR was 58.6 (25.4-101.7), and 145
reached kidney failure. eGFR was computed with the CKD-EPI creatinine equation;
kidney failure was defined as an eGFR of 10 mL/min/1.73 m^2 or less, the point
of dialysis initiation. Most participants (92%) were White. Each model was
fitted to a random 80% training split and checked against the remaining 20%.

The same information is available programmatically through the `population`
element of each model, e.g. `readModelDb("Ramesh_2025_adtkd_umod_egfr")()$population`.

## Model structure

**eGFR against age (Equation 1 and Supplementary S2).** For subject *i* at age
*a*,

  eGFR = DP0 * (1 - DPmax * f(a)),

where *f* is an asymmetric sigmoid in age: below the inflection age DPT50 it is
`(a/DPT50)^g1 / (1 + (a/DPT50)^g1)`, and above it `1 / (1 + (DPT50/a)^g2)`. The
two branches meet at 0.5 when `a = DPT50`, so the curve is continuous, but the
steepness changes from the shallow `g1` (about 1) to the steep `g2` (6.3 for
UMOD, 10.2 for MUC1). DP0 is the eGFR extrapolated to age 0, DPmax the maximum
fractional decrease (fixed), and log-normal random effects act on DPT50, `g1`,
`g2` and DP0, with `g1` and DP0 correlated. Continuous covariates enter as
power terms centred on the observation-weighted means printed in Supplementary
S2 (eGFR 43.4044 mL/min/1.73 m^2, age 35.2138 years).

**Age at kidney failure (Equation 2).** A Weibull hazard
`h(a) = (p/Te) * (a/Te)^(p - 1)`, so that the kidney-failure-free probability
is `S(a) = exp(-(a/Te)^p)` and `S(Te) = exp(-1) = 0.368` for every `p`
(Supplementary S1 Equation S3). Te carries an exponential effect of male sex
(UMOD only) and a power effect of the age at the first clinic visit. The files
store the Weibull scale as the rate `lambda = 1/Te` and rebuild Te in `model()`,
so the paper's covariate exponents keep their published signs.

## Structural verification

The eGFR model is algebraic, so a typical-value solve is compared against an
independent R implementation of Equation 1. Both sides use the same parameters,
so the bound is tight.

```{r egfr_closed_form}
egfr_closed <- function(age, e0, imax, t50, g1, g2) {
  f <- ifelse(
    age <= t50,
    (age / t50)^g1 / (1 + (age / t50)^g1),
    1 / (1 + (t50 / age)^g2)
  )
  e0 * (1 - imax * f)
}

cov_grid <- expand.grid(
  CRCL_BASE = c(15, 30, 45, 60, 90),
  AGE_BASE = c(20, 35, 50, 65)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())
age_grid <- seq(18, 85, by = 0.5)
typ_events <- cov_grid |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = age_grid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

solve_typical <- function(mod, label) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), typ_events, returnType = "data.frame",
                  keep = c("CRCL_BASE", "AGE_BASE")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(genotype = label)
}
typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  solve_typical(umod_egfr, "UMOD"),
  solve_typical(muc1_egfr, "MUC1")
)
closed <- with(typ, egfr_closed(time, e0, imax, t50max, hill, hill_late))
stopifnot(max(abs(typ$egfr - closed)) < 1e-8)

# Continuity at the inflection age: both branches give f = 0.5 there.
at_t50 <- typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(genotype, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    t50 = t50max[1], e0 = e0[1], imax = imax[1],
    g1 = hill[1], g2 = hill_late[1], .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    below = egfr_closed(t50 * (1 - 1e-9), e0, imax, t50, g1, g2),
    above = egfr_closed(t50 * (1 + 1e-9), e0, imax, t50, g1, g2)
  )
stopifnot(max(abs(at_t50$below - at_t50$above) / at_t50$e0) < 1e-6)
```

The Discussion notes that the near-unit exponent of the first-visit eGFR on
DP0 "ensur[es] consistency between clinical observations and model
predictions". That is checkable: for a typical subject, the eGFR the model
predicts at the age of the first visit should sit close to the eGFR measured at
that visit, across the whole covariate grid.

```{r first_visit_consistency}
first_visit <- typ |>
  dplyr::filter(abs(time - AGE_BASE) < 1e-8) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = egfr / CRCL_BASE)

first_visit |>
  dplyr::group_by(genotype) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `median ratio` = round(median(ratio), 3),
    `min ratio` = round(min(ratio), 3),
    `max ratio` = round(max(ratio), 3)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(Genotype = genotype) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical predicted eGFR at the first-visit age divided by the first-visit eGFR, over 20 covariate combinations.")

stopifnot(
  nrow(first_visit) == 40,
  all(abs(first_visit$ratio - 1) < 0.15)
)
```

The typical prediction at the first visit is within 15% of the measured
first-visit eGFR everywhere on the grid, a little below it because the shallow
pre-inflection branch has already lowered eGFR by the first visit.

For the time-to-event models the solved survival is compared against
`exp(-(age/Te)^p)`, and Equation S3 is checked: survival at age Te is
`exp(-1)` whatever the shape.

```{r kf_closed_form}
kf_events <- expand.grid(
  SEXF = c(0, 1),
  AGE_BASE = c(20, 35.2138, 50),
  time = seq(1, 90, by = 1)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(factor(paste(SEXF, AGE_BASE))), evid = 0, amt = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

# The time-to-event models have no random effects, so rxSolve() warns that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega; every subject is a typical subject here.
kf <- suppressWarnings(dplyr::bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(umod_kf, kf_events, returnType = "data.frame",
                  keep = c("SEXF", "AGE_BASE")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(genotype = "UMOD"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(muc1_kf, kf_events, returnType = "data.frame",
                  keep = c("SEXF", "AGE_BASE")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(genotype = "MUC1")
))
stopifnot(max(abs(kf$sur - exp(-(kf$time / kf$te)^kf$alfa))) < 1e-12)

at_te <- kf |>
  dplyr::distinct(genotype, SEXF, AGE_BASE, te, lam, alfa) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sur_te = exp(-(lam * te)^alfa))
stopifnot(max(abs(at_te$sur_te - exp(-1))) < 1e-12)
```

## Published derived quantities

The Discussion gives several numbers that follow from Table 2B.

```{r derived}
umod_te <- 54.32
umod_p <- 8.69
muc1_te <- 51.54
muc1_p <- 6.82
male_te <- umod_te * exp(-0.07)

derived <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Quantity, ~Model, ~Paper,
  "UMOD: Te for a male, years", male_te, 50.4,
  "UMOD: years by which males reach Te earlier", umod_te - male_te, 3.8,
  "UMOD: age at 50% KF-free, female, years", umod_te * log(2)^(1 / umod_p), 50,
  "UMOD: age at 50% KF-free, male, years", male_te * log(2)^(1 / umod_p), 46.5,
  "MUC1: age at 50% KF-free, years", muc1_te * log(2)^(1 / muc1_p), 48.3
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Model = round(Model, 2))
knitr::kable(derived, caption = "Discussion values against the packaged models at the reference covariates (age at first visit 35.2 years).")

stopifnot(
  abs(derived$Model[1] - 50.4) < 0.5,
  abs(derived$Model[2] - 3.8) < 0.5
)
```

The male Te and the four-year sex gap are reproduced. The ages at 50%
kidney-failure-free survival are 1-2 years above the Discussion's values for
UMOD and within a year for MUC1. The paper does not say at which age at first
visit those ages were computed; the model values above are at the centring age
of 35.2 years, and a 2-year shift corresponds to a first-visit age about 7
years younger, so the difference is not used as a gate.

## Kidney-failure-free survival by age at first visit (Figures 4 and 5)

Figures 4 and 5 are visual predictive checks stratified by sex (UMOD) and by
10-year bands of the age at the first clinic visit; the dashed line is the
model-predicted median. The age at which that dashed line crosses 0.5 was read
from each panel by the maintainers. The model value is the age at which the
mean survival over an even grid of first-visit ages across the band falls to
0.5. The digitised values carry about 1 year of reading error, and the
model-side band average assumes first-visit ages are spread evenly across the
band, which the registry cohort need not be.

```{r fig45}
band_median <- function(te0, p, b_male, b_age, male, lo, hi) {
  afcv <- seq(lo, hi, length.out = 41)
  te <- te0 * exp(b_male * male) * (afcv / 35.2138)^b_age
  uniroot(function(a) mean(exp(-(a / te)^p)) - 0.5, c(1, 150))$root
}

fig45 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Figure, ~Genotype, ~Sex, ~lo, ~hi, ~digitised,
  "4", "UMOD", "Female", 18, 28, 39.5,
  "4", "UMOD", "Male", 18, 28, 36,
  "4", "UMOD", "Female", 29, 38, 49.5,
  "4", "UMOD", "Male", 29, 38, 46,
  "4", "UMOD", "Female", 39, 48, 58.5,
  "4", "UMOD", "Male", 39, 48, 54.5,
  "5", "MUC1", "Both", 18, 28, 34.5,
  "5", "MUC1", "Both", 29, 38, 45.5,
  "5", "MUC1", "Both", 39, 48, 56,
  "5", "MUC1", "Both", 49, 58, 67,
  "5", "MUC1", "Both", 59, 72, 78
) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = if (Genotype == "UMOD") {
      band_median(umod_te, umod_p, -0.07, 0.59, as.numeric(Sex == "Male"), lo, hi)
    } else {
      band_median(muc1_te, muc1_p, 0, 0.81, 0, lo, hi)
    }
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = model - digitised)

fig45 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    band = paste0(lo, "-", hi),
    model = round(model, 1),
    diff = round(diff, 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Figure, Genotype, Sex, band, digitised, model, diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `First-visit age band` = band,
    `Figure median (years)` = digitised,
    `Model median (years)` = model,
    `Difference (years)` = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Age at which the predicted kidney-failure-free proportion reaches 0.5, by stratum.")

stopifnot(
  abs(median(fig45$diff)) < 1.5,
  max(abs(fig45$diff)) < 4
)
```

The model reproduces the stratum medians of both figures to within 1.7 years,
and to within a year in most strata. The largest gap is the oldest MUC1 band,
whose curve is cut off by the 80-year axis limit and whose 14-year band is the
widest, so the even-spread assumption matters most there. The model medians
sit slightly late overall, which is what a cohort whose first-visit ages
cluster toward the lower edge of each band would produce.

```{r fig45_plot, fig.height = 5}
curve_grid <- tidyr::crossing(
  fig45 |> dplyr::select(Genotype, Sex, lo, hi),
  age = seq(0, 90, by = 0.5)
) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sur = {
      afcv <- seq(lo, hi, length.out = 41)
      te <- if (Genotype == "UMOD") {
        umod_te * exp(-0.07 * (Sex == "Male")) * (afcv / 35.2138)^0.59
      } else {
        muc1_te * (afcv / 35.2138)^0.81
      }
      p <- if (Genotype == "UMOD") umod_p else muc1_p
      mean(exp(-(age / te)^p))
    }
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(panel = paste0(Genotype, ", ", lo, "-", hi, " years"))

ggplot(curve_grid, aes(age, sur, colour = Sex)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 4) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.2, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)", y = "Proportion free of kidney failure",
    title = "Typical survival by age at first clinic visit",
    caption = "Replicates the model-predicted medians of Figures 4 and 5 of Ramesh 2025."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Covariate effects on the eGFR trajectory (Figure 2)

Figure 2 shows the mean eGFR of simulated subjects for several first-visit eGFR
values (panels A and B) and first-visit ages (panels C and D), each subject
simulated with between-subject variability. The paper does not state the value
of the other covariate in each panel; here the first-visit age is 21 years in
panels A-B (the curves there start at about 21 years) and the first-visit eGFR
is the centring value in panels C-D. Each covariate value is simulated with 200
replicates and the mean is plotted.

```{r fig2, fig.height = 6}
n_rep <- 200
fig2_design <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(panel = "eGFR at first visit", level = c(15, 35, 55, 75, 95, 120),
                 CRCL_BASE = level, AGE_BASE = 21),
  tibble::tibble(panel = "Age at first visit", level = c(25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75),
                 CRCL_BASE = 43.4044, AGE_BASE = level)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(design = dplyr::row_number())

fig2_events <- fig2_design |>
  tidyr::crossing(rep = seq_len(n_rep)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number()) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(18, 100, by = 2)) |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= AGE_BASE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

sim_fig2 <- function(mod, label) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, fig2_events, returnType = "data.frame",
                  keep = c("panel", "level")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(panel, level, time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(egfr = mean(egfr), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(genotype = label)
}
fig2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_fig2(umod_egfr, "UMOD"),
  sim_fig2(muc1_egfr, "MUC1")
)

ggplot(fig2, aes(time, egfr, colour = factor(level), group = level)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_grid(panel ~ genotype) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)", y = "Mean eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)", colour = "Covariate",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Ramesh 2025 (panels A-D)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

As in Figure 2, a higher first-visit eGFR shifts the whole curve up and, through
the negative exponent on the post-inflection Hill coefficient, flattens the
late decline, while an older first-visit age delays the inflection. The panel
A-B curves start near their first-visit eGFR, as the paper's do.

## Virtual-cohort eGFR distribution (Figure 3)

Figure 3 is a visual predictive check of the training data. The registry's
visit schedule is not published, so a virtual cohort is used instead: 200
subjects per genotype, first-visit age and first-visit eGFR drawn
independently from log-normal distributions matching the Table 1 medians and
95% intervals (first-visit age truncated at 18 years), and annual visits for
9 years (the median follow-up). Residual error is included. The joint
distribution of the two covariates is not published.

```{r fig3_cohort}
draw_cohort <- function(n, age_med, age_lo, age_hi, egfr_med, egfr_lo, egfr_hi) {
  sd_age <- (log(age_hi) - log(age_lo)) / (2 * 1.96)
  sd_egfr <- (log(egfr_hi) - log(egfr_lo)) / (2 * 1.96)
  age <- exp(rnorm(n * 3, log(age_med), sd_age))
  age <- age[age >= 18][seq_len(n)]
  tibble::tibble(
    id = seq_len(n),
    AGE_BASE = age,
    CRCL_BASE = exp(rnorm(n, log(egfr_med), sd_egfr))
  )
}
visits <- function(cohort) {
  cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(year = 0:9) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = AGE_BASE + year, evid = 0, amt = 0) |>
    dplyr::select(-year) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time)
}
cohort_umod <- draw_cohort(200, 36.77, 18.34, 58.93, 45.35, 14.56, 94.83)
cohort_muc1 <- draw_cohort(200, 37.68, 20.56, 64.99, 58.63, 25.4, 101.74)

vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(umod_egfr, visits(cohort_umod), returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(genotype = "UMOD"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(muc1_egfr, visits(cohort_muc1), returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(genotype = "MUC1")
)

vpc_bins <- vpc |>
  dplyr::mutate(age_bin = cut(time, breaks = c(18, 27, 35, 41, 47, 53, 59, 70))) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(age_bin)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(genotype, age_bin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    age = median(time),
    p10 = quantile(sim, 0.1),
    p50 = median(sim),
    p90 = quantile(sim, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc_bins, aes(age)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  facet_wrap(~genotype) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 120)) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)", y = "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)",
    caption = "Median and 10th-90th percentiles of a virtual cohort; compare Figure 3 of Ramesh 2025."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Figure 3's predicted median falls from about 49 mL/min/1.73 m^2 at age 23 to
about 20 at age 63 for UMOD, and from about 51 at age 27 to about 30 at age 66
for MUC1. The virtual cohort does **not** reproduce that fall: its median stays
between about 34 and 47 across the age bins. The reason is the cohort, not the
model. Because the first-visit eGFR scales DP0 almost proportionally (exponent
1 for UMOD, 0.96 for MUC1), each subject's trajectory is anchored to the eGFR
they arrive with, and the population fall with age in Figure 3 comes from the
registry's patients arriving later in life with lower eGFR. The paper reports
the two first-visit covariates only as separate marginal summaries, so the
virtual cohort draws them independently, and its older subjects enter with the
same eGFR distribution as its younger ones. Within each subject the decline is
as the model prescribes (Figure 2 above); the plot is shown to make this
dependence on the input cohort explicit, and it is not used as a gate.

## Assumptions and deviations

* **Model time is age.** The eGFR models use age at the visit as the Monolix
  regressor and the kidney-failure models use the age at the event, so the
  packaged models take age in the `time` column. Neither model is meant for
  ages below 18 years (Discussion).
* **DPmax = 0.999, not 0.99.** Table 2A and the Results print 0.99, while the
  Supplementary S2 project fixes `Imax_pop` to 0.999. A fixed value in a Monolix
  project is the value the fit used, so the model carries 0.999. The difference
  changes the late-life eGFR floor `DP0 * (1 - DPmax)` from 0.8 to 0.08
  mL/min/1.73 m^2 and is invisible above the kidney-failure threshold.
* **Supplementary S2 parameter values are initial values.** The `<PARAMETER>`
  blocks of the Monolix projects differ from Table 2 on every estimated value
  (e.g. UMOD `IC50_pop` 38.95 vs 39.76, Te_pop 64.29 vs 54.32, p_pop 20 vs
  8.69), and the two time-to-event projects carry a covariate model (UMOD:
  sub-mutation family and sex; MUC1: none) that is not the final one in Table
  2B. All estimates are therefore from Table 2, with the structure, the
  centring values and the fixed DPmax from Supplementary S2.
* **IIV variances from the %CV.** Table 2A prints each omega as an SD to one or
  two decimals with the %CV in brackets. The variances are `log(1 + CV^2)`,
  which reproduces each printed SD to its rounding except UMOD gamma2 (printed
  0.8; the 98.93% CV implies 0.826).
* **Correlation partner.** The MUC1 Results text says the -0.63 correlation is
  between gamma1 and "DP50", but Table 2A and the Supplementary S2 project both
  place it between gamma1 and DP0, which is used.
* **Centring of the age at first visit in the kidney-failure models.** Table 2B
  footnote points to the weighted-mean centring of Equation S1 but the centring
  value of the time-to-event covariate is not printed. The models use the
  35.2138 years printed for the same covariate in the eGFR projects; Figures 4
  and 5 are reproduced with it.
* **Survival from birth.** The time-to-event models give the probability of
  being free of kidney failure from birth, as the Figure 4-5 predicted curves
  do. The probability of remaining free beyond a later age `a0`, given freedom
  at `a0`, is `sur(a) / sur(a0)`.
* **Censoring.** eGFR values below 10 mL/min/1.73 m^2 were handled as censored
  (M4) in the fit. The packaged model simulates eGFR without censoring, and the
  residual error can give values below zero for a very low prediction.
* **No PKNCA.** There is no drug and no concentration, so NCA does not apply;
  validation uses the closed forms and the paper's figures and Discussion
  values instead.
* **Virtual cohort.** The first-visit age and eGFR are drawn independently
  because only their marginal medians and 95% intervals are published; see the
  Figure 3 section for the consequence.
* **Covariate canonical names.** eGFR at the first clinic visit is carried as
  `CRCL_BASE` (time-fixed baseline renal function, mL/min/1.73 m^2) and the
  age at the first visit as `AGE_BASE`, a time-fixed baseline age distinct from
  the current age, which is the model time.
